page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-48 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. It is configured with 378.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per virtual core. This high memory-to-CPU ratio is designed to support memory-intensive workloads that require substantial memory capacity relative to compute resources.

The instance does not include any local NVMe SSD storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage options. Additionally, the c4d-highmem-48 does not feature any hardware accelerators or GPUs, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. These hardware constraints represent a tradeoff, positioning the server specifically for workloads that do not require local high-speed disk access or GPU acceleration.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high memory density provide a stable environment for memory-bound applications without the overhead of unused GPU hardware. The instance is suited for workloads such as medium-to-large databases, in-memory caching systems, enterprise resource planning applications, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
